title: What is Margin Trading Facility (MTF) and Why is SEBI Reviewing It?
description: The Margin Trading Facility (MTF) lets you buy more shares than your available cash by borrowing funds from your stockbroker. You pay a portion of the total s.

faq.q: Who can offer Margin Trading Facility (MTF)?
faq.a: Only SEBI-registered stockbrokers who are members of recognised stock exchanges like NSE and BSE, and who meet specific eligibility criteria (like having a minimum net worth, currently proposed to be ₹5 crore), can offer MTF.

faq.q: Which stocks are eligible for MTF?
faq.a: Generally, only certain equity shares and units of Equity ETFs classified as 'Group I securities' by SEBI are eligible for margin trading. The list of eligible securities is updated periodically.

A margin call happens when the value of the shares you bought using MTF (which are pledged as collateral) falls, reducing your effective margin below the required level. Your broker will then ask you to deposit additional funds or collateral to cover this shortfall.

faq.q: Is there a minimum margin I need to pay?
faq.a: Yes, SEBI mandates that clients must provide a minimum initial margin of 25% of the total purchase value of the MTF trade from their own funds or eligible collateral. Brokers can also ask for higher margins based on their risk assessment.

faq.q: How long can I hold shares under MTF?
faq.a: You can hold shares purchased under MTF for as long as you wish, provided you continuously maintain the required margin with your broker and pay the applicable interest charges. There is no fixed maximum holding period like in intraday trading.
